screens.name: 01-simple-today
screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: polished Android mobile habit and daily routine app redesign concept. Generate ONE portrait image containing ONE large front-facing Android phone screen with narrow charcoal bezel, tiny centered circular hole-punch camera, slim Android status bar 9:41 and bottom gesture bar, on a simple warm off-white background. No iPhone notch or dynamic island, no perspective angle, no hands, no extra screens or marketing headings. Show the entire screen with comfortable margins, crisp highly legible English interface text. All four concept screens share this exact design language: warm ivory #F8F7F3 background, forest green #24584A primary action, pale sage #E8EEE5 minimal highlights, tiny warm amber accents, dark charcoal text, subtle hairline dividers, clean sans-serif typography, 24px content margins, moderate rounded corners, large accessible tap targets, calm flat professional UI. The purpose is SIMPLICITY and obvious next actions: generous whitespace, concise labels, one main action per area, no noisy dashboard, no large decorative illustration, no gradients, no heavy shadows, no competing colored panels. User explicitly wants notifications excluded: no reminders, bell icons, notification switches, snooze, permission UI. Use consistent example habit Read a book with 20-minute goal, scheduled 9:00 PM. Treat this as a new improved concept, not an existing app screenshot.
Today screen. Header large "Today" with small "Friday, October 16" and one settings gear at upper right. Below: minimal 7-day strip Mon12 Tue13 Wed14 Thu15 Fri16 Sat17 Sun18 with Fri16 selected green. A compact flat sage progress panel shows only "3 of 5 completed" and a thin 60% bar. Section "Still to do" with TWO compact ivory task rows separated by hairlines, no big nested cards: book icon, "Read a book", "9:00 PM · 10 / 20 min", a small green outlined "Add" button on right and a quiet ellipsis; dumbbell icon, "Evening workout", "6:00 PM · 20 min", a large empty completion circle on right and quiet ellipsis. A single collapsed disclosure row "Completed · 3" with chevron, no completed cards expanded. A small subtle row "Your routines" with sunrise icon and chevron. Lots of breathing room. ONE large forest green bottom button "+ New habit". Bottom navigation icons AND labels "Today" selected, "Schedule", "Progress". Do not add any second plus button, stats grid, busy-day switch, slogans, missed/skipped counters, badges, or extra sections. Goal is visibly simpler than a dense habit dashboard.

Create habit screen with streamlined short form. Top left back arrow and header "New habit". Four easy plain-language sections ONLY, with generous space and simple thin bordered fields: "What will you do?" input with small book icon and value "Read a book"; "How much?" three compact segmented options "Check off", "Minutes" selected green, "Count", followed by large inline "20" and "minutes"; "Which days?" a single selection field "Every day" with calendar outline icon and chevron; "When?" a time field "9:00 PM" with clock outline icon and chevron, and a quiet inline option "Anytime". Below a collapsed row "More options" with down chevron, helper text "Icon, category, start date, busy-day goal". Do not expand these additional settings. Place ONE full-width forest green "Create habit" button near screen bottom. No bottom tabs here. No oversized icon gallery, no date-format text inputs, no reminder option, no excessive chips. The screen should feel fast and easy for a first-time user, with most form visible without scrolling.
